title: 13th Parliamentary Election
subtitle: Bangladesh's Election Commission set the parliamentary election and referendum for 12 February 2026 amid a transition-period political reset.
summary: On 11 December 2025, Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin announced that Bangladesh's 13th National Parliamentary Election and a national referendum would be held on 12 February 2026. International and domestic attention then focused on election management, participation, and confidence in the process.
heroTagline: The central question became whether institutions, parties, and observers would view the process as inclusive and credible.
whyItMatters: UN technical support and international observation became part of the election environment: UN support was reported as ongoing since December 2024 at the Election Commission's request, and the EU deployed an Election Observation Mission following an official invitation. These steps made process quality, not only polling-day logistics, a major public benchmark.
longTermLegacy: The 2026 cycle is likely to be judged over time by whether the rules, participation conditions, and oversight practices were seen as durable beyond one election date.
identityMemoryNotes: As of February 2026, public framing around the 13th election emphasized process credibility, inclusion, and monitoring capacity rather than only formal scheduling milestones.

claimCitations.claim: On 11 December 2025, Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin announced that Bangladesh's 13th National Parliamentary Election and a national referendum would be held on 12 February 2026.
UN support was reported as ongoing since December 2024 at the Election Commission's request, and the EU deployed an Election Observation Mission following an official invitation.
A UN briefing to political parties on 4 December 2025 described technical support activities including voter registration expansion and operational support to the Election Commission.
The 2026 cycle is likely to be judged over time by whether the rules, participation conditions, and oversight practices were seen as durable beyond one election date.
As of February 2026, public framing around the 13th election emphasized process credibility, inclusion, and monitoring capacity rather than only formal scheduling milestones.
